lines: Training yard on the green, is it? Good. Tell Hale I said the stove goes on the north side, out of the wind.
You'll want a ring in Crossroads too, now. Somewhere to practise that isn't my doorstep.
Restore the old one on the green. I'll send down how we built the hut's: a stove beside it, always lit.
Tam's sitting by my stove, and I'm sitting next to her. Both of us. Sitting.
Go and say hello. She's been asking for you.
Take the shard down to your town's lantern. Tam will be along when her hands warm up.
You found Tam? Thank the hills.
Take that light down off my mountain. Carefully. It's colder than it looks.
The ice-cutter's by the tarn. She saw the light go under the glacier, and Tam right after it.
The caves are under the glacier's snout, past the crevasse trod. Keep to the blue ice. The white ice breaks.
The fells are clear? Then I can open the ring again, and you can hear the rest.
The light that fell up here slid under the glacier. Tam went in after it, the night of the starfall.
Tam came up here to sit in the snow and think. She's stubborn and she's warm-blooded. Go and fetch her.
The ibex are up on the High Fells, on the bench past the boulder field. They're not mean. They're frightened.
Use the boulders. Let them come to you.
Bread! Real bread, from Moss! Sit down. No, the bench, I'll stand. I always stand.
Since the storm I've kept the hut open on my own. Kettle on, door open, ring shut.
The ring stays shut till the fells are safe. The ibex up there have gone wild. Free them and we'll talk.
The hut is always open. The kettle is always on. Mind the step; it has opinions about boots.
The tarn's quiet again. Quiet enough to hear the ice sing at night. It never used to do that.
The night of the storm a light came down on the glacier and slid, like a stone on a frozen pond.
It went in under the snout. A blue mouth in the ice, at the end of the crevasse trod.
Tam went in after it with nothing but her beads. Bring her back, will you?
I cut ice for the inn at Cogsworth. Or I did, before the line went down. Now I just cut ice.
The choughs gave my baskets back. Well, they dropped them. Same thing.
The choughs over the cirque took my baskets, every one. Birds with baskets. I ask you.
Kettle's on. Sit when you can. Stand when you must. That's all the wisdom I have today.
The warden sat down. She actually sat down, with a cup, and didn't get up for the whole cup.
The fells are quiet, the shard is gone, and the warden has me to argue with now.
So the hut doesn't need me as much as I thought. But you might. Can I walk with you a while?
The light is yours now. Take it somewhere warm. I'll follow when my hands remember how to be hands.
You came in. Good. I've been holding the cold back from the light with my palms, and my palms are tired.
It's quiet now. Thank you for freeing the old wyrm. It was only cold and scared, like me.
Take the shard. I'll come out behind you.
Breathe in. Breathe out. Then go gently.
The hollow in the ice where the shard was is already filling with snow.
The great shard is frozen into the chamber wall. When you touch it the ice lets go at once, as if it was waiting.
